explain.say: Here is a party plan. Say happy birthday and give your gift. Join a game. Take a break if you need one. Say thank you. You can do it! Your challenge: practise your thank you words with a grown-up.

faq.q: What if the party is too busy for me?
faq.a: You can take a break in a quiet spot, wear ear defenders, or stay for a shorter time. A grown-up you trust can help you plan.
asks: Tell me about Lots of people

faq.q: How does the birthday child feel?
faq.a: Usually happy and special. Coming to their party shows you care about them.
asks: Tell me about Leo feels happy

faq.q: Can I take a break at a party?
faq.a: Yes. You can say, Is there a quiet place I can sit? Then come back when you feel ready.
asks: Tell me about A quiet break
Tell me about Take a break

faq.q: What do I say when I leave a party?
faq.a: You can say, Thank you for having me, and Happy birthday! A wave works too.
asks: Tell me about Say thank you
Tell me about Thank you, bye!

faq.q: What if I do not like the party food?
faq.a: That is okay. You can say, No, thank you. A grown-up might pack a snack you like.
asks: I do not like the food

facts: Birthday songs and traditions are different around the world.
In Mexico, many birthday parties have a piñata filled with sweets.

quiz.say: The party feels too loud. What can you ask?
quiz.show: Too loud. What can you ask?
quiz.why: A quiet place gives you a short break. Then you can join in again.

wrong.1: It is the birthday child's party, so everyone stays.
wrong.2: Asking helps a grown-up help you.

quiz.say: How does Leo feel when Sofia comes?
quiz.why: Coming to his party shows Sofia cares, so Leo feels special.
